channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: OpenAI Agent Hacked Australian Government Website, Albanese Says
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent hacked a government website, adding that the firm’s Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman had acknowledged the lapse.
item.dc:creator: Ainsley Thomson

item.title: Altman, Amodei Call on UN, World Leaders to Boost AI Safety
item.description: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman and Anthropic PBC CEO Dario Amodei urged world leaders to work together on artificial intelligence in an extraordinary appearance before the United Nations Security Council that focused on growing concerns the technology poses existential risks to humanity.
item.dc:creator: Magdalena Del Valle

item.title: Trump Jr.’s 1789 Capital in Talks to Raise $3 Billion in New Funds
item.description: Investment firm 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, is in talks to raise $3 billion for its second growth fund, according to a person familiar with the matter, bolstering its push to make larger bets on startups.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Apple Explores Screenless Fitness Tracker to Rival Whoop
item.description: Apple is exploring a new screenless health and fitness tracker designed to compete with devices from Whoop and Oura, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports. The device could offer longer battery life and make sleep and workout tracking easier than with an Apple Watch. Gurman discusses the project as part of a broader rethink of Apple’s wearables lineup, alongside new smart-home products, smart glasses and other devices in development. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessemer: Anthropic Has Been Consistent on AI Safety
item.description: Bessemer Venture Partners has raised $5.75 billion in fresh capital, its largest fundraise ever, including $4 billion dedicated to growth-stage investments as AI companies raise larger rounds and remain private for longer. Partner Sameer Dholakia discusses why the firm sees a “special moment” for investing across AI applications and physical AI, its early bet on Anthropic, and why he believes intelligence could ultimately become an economic input comparable to oil. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Agents Fuel a New Cybersecurity Boom
item.description: As AI shifts from technology that talks to technology that acts, Rosenblatt Securities Analyst Catharine Trebnick says securing autonomous agents is becoming a major new opportunity for cybersecurity companies. She discusses growing demand for products from CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks that track AI agents, identities and permissions, and explains why increasingly capable frontier models are more likely to strengthen established cybersecurity platforms. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Morgan Stanley’s Jonas: Physical AI Could Multiply Global GDP
item.description: Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas says the convergence of AI and robotics could have a transformational impact on the global economy, potentially multiplying GDP as physical AI spreads across transportation, manufacturing and everyday life. He discusses why the robotics race is inseparable from rebuilding US manufacturing, where China holds an advantage across key supply chains, and how Tesla and SpaceX could play complementary roles in a future where billions of connected robots perform more AI inference at the edge. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: From Anthropic to Robots: AI’s Next Frontier
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Anthropic's new faster, cheaper AI model as the startup tries to stay ahead of rivals before its IPO. Plus, Morgan Stanley's Adam Jonas discusses SpaceX, Tesla and the robotics boom, and Bloomberg reports Apple aims to take on Whoop with its own screenless health and fitness tracker. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft President Backs Deployment of AI Safety Evaluators
item.description: Microsoft Corp. President Brad Smith said the company backs the use of independent evaluators for artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day and Ed Ludlow

item.title: AI Safety Won't Advance If We Rely On Two Companies, Says Smith
item.description: Microsoft will spend $10 billion through 2030 in four Persian Gulf countries. The software giant will build out infrastructure and strengthen cyber security. Microsoft President Brad Smith spoke with Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow to discuss. He also spoke about AI saying that AI safety won't advance if we rely on two companies as well the need for independent evaluators. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Customizable AI Models Are Enabling Hackers to Conduct Cybercrime Sprees
item.description: It’s an emerging risk.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Howell O'Neill

item.title: Nvidia Is Shaping the Rules for AI
item.description: Jensen Huang and Donald Trump have become comrades in downplaying AI warnings and fighting back against new regulation. Bloomberg Opinion columnis Parmy Olson says that slowing down development just isn’t an option for Nvidia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta AI Disrupts the Tech Race, Morgan Stanleys's Deal Leak
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Diplomacy in New York raises hopes for an Iran breakthrough. Plus, Morgan Stanley’s confidential deal leak, Royal Caribbean’s $3 billion Sandals bet, and the CEOs of PG&E and Ben & Jerry’s join Bloomberg Open Interest in the C-Suite. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft, BofA, Macquarie on AI Infrastructure
item.description: William Demas, Senior Managing Director & Head of Americas, Green Investment Group, Macquarie Asset Management; Karen Fang, Global Head, Infrastructure & Sustainable Finance & Co-Head, Global Capital Solutions, Bank of America; and Melanie Nakagawa, Chief Sustainability Officer, Microsoft discuss AI infrastructure investments with Bloomberg's Lauren Smart at Bloomberg Green New York 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Amazon Sustainability Chief on Community Impact
item.description: Kara Hurst, Chief Sustainability Officer, Amazon discusses disaster relief, water stewardship and community impact with Bloomberg's Carol Massar at Bloomberg Green New York 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: If the US Slows Down on AI, China Wins, Says Ives
item.description: Xi Jinping and Donald Trump will sit down this week to hash out a plethora of thorny issues from trade to Taiwan. One thing both sides agree on: neither can afford to tap the brakes on AI. Dan Ives, Partner and Senior Managing Director, Analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co. joins Paul and Scarlet to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: FBI Investigating Hackers’ Claims of Stealing Employee Data
item.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is probing hackers’ claims that they broke into the agency’s systems and stole thousands of current and former employees’ data, the bureau said in a statement Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Jake Bleiberg and Ryan Gallagher

item.title: SoftBank Pays Steep Price to Become Goliath of Junk-Bond Markets
item.description: Billionaire Masayoshi Son’s SoftBank Group Corp. pushed through one of the largest junk-bond offerings on record, dangling yields above anything it’s paid before in an effort to fund its massive AI ambitions.
item.dc:creator: Janice Huang, Harry Suhartono, Ronan Martin and Gowri Gurumurthy

item.title: Whole Foods CEO: Customers Are Making More Trips
item.description: Whole Foods CEO Jason Buechel came into the studio to speak with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick about Amazon's approach to affordability, how customer's are changing shopping habits amid rising costs and how the healthy grocery competition has changed. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ari Emanuel Dishes on Hollywood Feuds, Paramount Merger and Elon Musk Friendship
item.description: A conversation with the pugilistic and hyperactive media mogul about his new memoir ‘Roll the Calls’
item.dc:creator: Lucas Shaw
